claims.text: The London Eye, originally known as the Millennium Wheel, is an enormous cantilevered observation wheel located right on the South Bank of the River Thames.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: It stands an impressive 135 metres tall and the wheel itself has a massive diameter of 120 metres.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: When it first opened to the public in 2000, it held the title of the world's tallest Ferris wheel until 2006.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Unlike taller traditional wheels, the London Eye is cantilevered, meaning it is supported solely by a giant A-frame on just one side.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The wheel carries 32 exterior glass-walled capsules that slowly rotate to provide panoramic sights.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: On a clear, good day, the sweeping views from the top can stretch up to 40 km away over central London.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Today, it is actually the most popular paid tourist attraction in the United Kingdom, drawing more than three million visitors annually.
claims.subject: self
